learningObjectives.title: Indian, African, Middle Eastern and Latin American music

questions.q: Which instrument is a pair of small hand drums used in Indian classical music?
questions.explain: The tabla is a pair of tuned hand drums central to North Indian classical music.

questions.q: What is a tala in Indian classical music?
options: A repeating rhythmic cycle of a set number of beats
A melodic scale used for improvisation
A drone sustained throughout the piece
questions.explain: The tala provides the rhythmic framework, organising the music into a repeating cycle of beats.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the framework of notes used for melody and improvisation is called the:
questions.explain: The raga is the melodic basis of the music, providing the notes for improvisation.

questions.q: Teental is a widely used tala. How many beats does its cycle contain?
questions.explain: Teental is a 16-beat cycle, usually grouped as 4+4+4+4.

questions.q: The djembe, a rope-tuned goblet drum, originates from which region?
questions.explain: The djembe is a hand-played goblet drum from West Africa.

questions.q: Which term describes several independent rhythms played at the same time, as heard in African drumming?
questions.explain: Polyrhythm is the simultaneous layering of two or more contrasting rhythms.

questions.q: In African music, 'call and response' refers to:
options: A leader's phrase answered by the rest of the group
Two identical rhythms played in unison
questions.explain: Call and response alternates a soloist's phrase with an answering group, common across African music.

questions.q: Which goblet-shaped hand drum is characteristic of Middle Eastern music?
questions.explain: The darbuka (or doumbek) is a goblet-shaped drum widely used in Middle Eastern music.

questions.q: The system of melodic modes used in Middle Eastern (Arabic) music is known as:
questions.explain: A maqam is a melodic mode that governs the notes and character of Middle Eastern music.

questions.q: The oud, widely used in Middle Eastern music, is best described as a:
questions.explain: The oud is a short-necked, fretless plucked string instrument, an ancestor of the European lute.

questions.q: Samba is a style of music and dance originating in:
questions.explain: Samba developed in Brazil and is strongly associated with Rio de Janeiro's carnival.

questions.q: In a samba band, which large drum provides the steady underlying pulse?
questions.explain: The surdo is the large bass drum that marks the basic pulse of the samba band.

questions.q: In samba, the term 'bateria' refers to:
questions.explain: The bateria is the large percussion ensemble that drives a samba performance.

questions.q: Which repeating two-bar rhythmic pattern underpins much Latin American music such as salsa?
questions.explain: The clave is a syncopated two-bar rhythmic pattern that acts as the backbone of much Latin American music.

questions.q: Syncopation is best described as:
options: Placing accents on normally weak beats or offbeats
Playing every note on the main beats
questions.explain: Syncopation stresses beats or parts of beats that are normally weak, creating rhythmic interest.

questions.q: In compound time, each main beat is divided into:
questions.explain: In compound time each beat subdivides into three, unlike simple time where it divides into two.

questions.q: You hear music with two dotted-crotchet beats per bar, each dividing into three quavers (6/8). What metre is this?
questions.explain: Two beats per bar (duple) each split into three (compound) gives compound duple time, notated as 6/8.

questions.q: A recording features surdo, tamborim and agogô playing fast, syncopated interlocking rhythms. Which style is it most likely to be?
questions.explain: The surdo, tamborim and agogô are core instruments of the Brazilian samba bateria.

questions.q: A piece begins with a slow, unmetred, improvised melody over a drone before the tabla enters. What is this opening section called?
questions.explain: The alap is the free, unmetred opening of an Indian classical performance, before the rhythmic tala begins.

questions.q: During an African drumming ensemble, one player signals changes and leads the other drummers. This musician is known as the:
questions.explain: The master drummer directs the ensemble, cueing changes in rhythm and dynamics.
